guide_enrichment.narrative:
Our numbers give USC a modest underlying advantage, largely because we trust its ability to create scoring opportunities more than Wisconsin’s. USC averaged 6.9 yards per play and converted 56% of its third downs through five games, with Jayden Maiava completing 70.1% of his passes and producing 16 total touchdowns. That efficiency helps explain why our expectation sits slightly above the broader market view.

We are not treating the Oregon result as proof of anything, but it highlights both sides of the USC profile. USC erased a 10-point second-half deficit before losing 41-27, showing its ability to generate sustained scoring drives while again leaving questions about finishing games. USC allowed 57 fourth-quarter points through five contests, its highest total in any quarter.

For us, the hesitation is the price rather than the basic matchup case. USC’s rushing profile does not create the same advantage as its overall scoring-opportunity production, and the available number already accounts for our modest preference. We can see why USC is favored without seeing enough remaining value to make this a wager.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: We are watching USC’s passing offense against Wisconsin’s scoring-opportunity prevention. Maiava had thrown 14 touchdowns against two interceptions through five games, and USC had allowed only five sacks while averaging 489.4 total yards. If that combination of accuracy and protection continues, USC should have chances to reach scoring range consistently; the question for our view is whether those possessions produce enough separation to justify the market’s demand.

recent_game.fact: USC lost 41-27 at home to Oregon on Sept. 26, falling to 4-1 overall and 1-1 in Big Ten play.
Against Oregon, USC quarterback Jayden Maiava completed 23 of 42 passes for 326 yards and two touchdowns and added a 1-yard rushing touchdown.
Maiava led scoring drives of 75, 63 and 75 yards as USC erased a 20-10 third-quarter deficit and tied Oregon 27-27 early in the fourth quarter.
Freshman wide receiver Kayden Dixon-Wyatt had career highs of seven receptions and 114 yards against Oregon, including a 31-yard touchdown.
Running back King Miller led USC against Oregon with 74 rushing yards on 13 carries, while Waymond Jordan added 41 yards on nine carries.
USC recorded four tackles for loss against Oregon; defensive tackle Jahkeem Stewart had two, tying his single-game career high.

opponent_notes.fact: USC is scheduled to play at Wisconsin on Oct. 24, 2026, following a bye on Oct. 17.

quarterback.fact: Through five games, Jayden Maiava had completed 110 of 157 passes for 1,499 yards, 14 touchdowns and two interceptions, with a 70.1% completion rate and 174.5 efficiency rating.
Maiava had accounted for 16 touchdowns through five games, with 14 passing and two rushing.
Maiava had two 300-yard passing games through USC's first five contests.

offensive_personnel.fact: Kayden Dixon-Wyatt led USC through five games with 25 receptions and 372 receiving yards and had three touchdowns, averaging 14.9 yards per catch.
Freshman tight end Mark Bowman ranked second on USC with 21 receptions and had 204 receiving yards and two touchdowns through five games.
King Miller had 412 rushing yards through five games after gaining 74 yards against Oregon.
USC had allowed five sacks through its first five games while averaging 489.4 total yards per game.

defensive_personnel.fact: Linebacker Deven Bryant and safety Christian Pierce tied for USC's team lead against Oregon with seven tackles each.
Defensive tackle Jahkeem Stewart returned to the Coliseum against Oregon and recorded two tackles for loss.
Cornerbacks Chasen Johnson and Prophet Brown each recorded a pass breakup against Oregon.
